summary: Reviewed the new verification-integrity gate (check-verification-integrity.py, CODEOWNERS, CI job, project-baseline refactor, tests, contract). The suppression-detection forms, exact-move alignment, CODEOWNERS last-match coverage, CI base selection, and the baseline-check refactor all behave as documented. The one defect class found is in V5 self-comparison detection: in all three language scanners the assertEquals/assertEqual/assert.equal family only flags the two-argument form, so the extremely common message-overload form (assertEquals(expected, expected, "message") and equivalents) silently evades the constant/self-comparing assertion rule while preserving the assertion count that V4 checks.

findings.title: Java V5 self-comparison check misses the 3-arg message overload
findings.trigger: A PR replaces a real assertion in an existing Java test with assertEquals(expected, expected, "message") or assertSame(value, value, "message") — the standard JUnit overload carrying a failure message — keeping the test's assertion count unchanged.
findings.consequence: The gate reports no violation (exit 0) even though a constant self-comparing assertion was added, violating the documented V5 rule; the test is silently weakened with V4 unable to see it because the assertion count is preserved.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:302 requires len(original) == 2 before comparing original[0] == original[1], so any 3-arg assertEquals/assertSame is skipped; the adjacent assertTrue/assertFalse branches at lines 300-301 explicitly handle the message overload via values[0]/values[-1], showing the arity restriction here is an oversight rather than a documented limitation (the contract at verification/verification-integrity.md states V5 covers self-comparing assertions without an arity qualification).
findings.suggestedFix: Compare the first two arguments regardless of trailing message/delta arguments: change the condition to len(original) >= 2 and original[0] == original[1], and add regressions for assertEquals(x, x, "msg") and assertSame(x, x, "msg").

findings.title: Python V5 self-comparison check misses the 3-arg message form
findings.trigger: A PR adds self.assertEqual(value, value, "message") or self.assertIs(value, value, "message") to an existing Python test while removing another assertion, keeping the per-test assertion count constant.
findings.consequence: The new self-comparing assertion is not flagged as V5 and the count-based V4 check sees no reduction, so the gate passes (exit 0) on a weakened test despite the documented V5 contract covering self-comparing assertions.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:375 gates the ast.dump equality comparison on len(node.args) == 2; unittest's assertEqual/assertIs accept an optional third msg argument, so the idiomatic message form escapes detection. The neighboring assertTrue/assertFalse branch at line 372-373 inspects args[0] without an arity cap, confirming the inconsistency.
findings.suggestedFix: Relax the check to len(node.args) >= 2 and compare node.args[0] with node.args[1]; add regressions for assertEqual(v, v, "msg") and assertIs(v, v, "msg").

findings.title: TypeScript V5 self-comparison check misses the message overload of node assert
findings.trigger: A PR adds assert.equal(value, value, "message") or assert.strictEqual(value, value, "message") to an existing TypeScript test while deleting another assertion, keeping the assertion count for the test case unchanged.
findings.consequence: The self-comparing assertion evades the V5 check and V4 sees no count change, so the integrity gate exits 0 on a silently weakened test, contrary to the documented V5 rule.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:477-481 computes the noop only when len(original) == 2 and original[0] == original[1]; node's assert.equal/strictEqual/deepEqual/deepStrictEqual all accept a trailing message argument, which makes the common 3-arg form invisible to the scanner.
findings.suggestedFix: Drop the len(original) == 2 requirement in favor of len(original) >= 2 comparing the first two arguments, and add regressions for assert.strictEqual(v, v, "msg") and assert.deepEqual(v, v, "msg").
